mechanism_log: The system has exactly 6 active inputs (X1–X6) and 6 completely inactive inputs (X7–X12). Each output has a sparse causal structure: Y1 is driven positively by all of X1–X6 (with X5 showing a hard threshold/saturation above ~0.55); Y2 is increased by X2 and X6 (bad for minimization) and decreased by X1, X3, X4 (good); Y3 (threshold ≥0.4) is driven ONLY by X1 and X3; Y4 is driven positively by X2 and X4 and negatively by X6. There are potential interactions between X2 and X4 (gradients flip sign at high joint values for Y2), and between X1 and X3 for Y3. The core tradeoff is that X6 helps Y1 but hurts Y2 and Y4, and X2 helps Y1/Y4 but slightly hurts Y2.

The system has 6 active inputs (X1–X6) and 6 completely inactive inputs (X7–X12). The system is highly multiplicative/nonlinear — linear additive assumptions fail at extreme input combinations. Key structure: Y1 is driven positively by all of X1–X6 (X5 threshold-saturates above ~0.55); Y2 is primarily driven UP by X2 (main harmful driver) and DOWN by X3, X1, X4 (at low X2), but X4 and X6 REVERSE their signs on Y2 depending on X2 level — a strong regime-dependent interaction; Y3 (constraint ≥0.4) is controlled solely by X1 and X3, easily satisfied at X1=X3=1; Y4 is driven up by X2 and X4, down by X6. The Pareto frontier is a 2D surface in (X2, X6) space with X1=X3=X4=1, X5=0.6 fixed. The hypervolume improved from 0.136 to 0.252 through targeted optimization revealing Y1 range up to 1.129 and Y2 as low as 0.071.
